default.title: FRIEND AGAIN
default.speaker: Friend
default.text: The friend who borrowed ₹500 hasn't paid it back, and now asks for ₹300 more.

choices.lesson: Lending more to someone who hasn't repaid only deepens the hole. Save first; lend only what you can lose.

effects.label: Got ₹250 back, the rest next week

choices.lesson: Asking for your own money back is fair. Your savings plan comes first.
Good. The ₹500 may be gone, but you stopped the leak.

default.title: WEDDING GIFT
default.speaker: Mom
default.text: Your cousin's wedding is next week. The family expects you to chip in ₹150 for the gift.

effects.label: Gift money from the fun budget

choices.lesson: Planned spending absorbs surprises. Cutting wants this week kept your needs safe.
That works, but savings are for goals and emergencies. Next time keep a small 'family events' line in the plan.
Borrowing for a gift means paying more for it later.

default.title: DATA OVER
default.speaker: Your phone
default.text: Data's finished. Pack A: ₹199 for 28 days. Pack B: ₹19 a day. Which costs less for the month?

choices.lesson: ₹19 × 28 days = ₹532. The monthly pack costs less than half. Divide before you decide.
₹19 feels cheap, but 28 of them is ₹532. Small daily costs add up.

default.title: QUIZ PRIZE!
default.speaker: Principal
default.text: You won the college quiz! The prize: ₹200 cash.

choices.lesson: Celebrate and save: a split keeps you happy now and gets you closer to your goal.
Your goal jar just jumped! A small treat is allowed too.
Fun! Next time, try putting part of a surprise windfall towards your goal.

default.title: PRICE HIKE
default.speaker: Canteen anna
default.text: 'Samosa ₹12 from today, tea ₹10.' Your pocket money is the same as last year.

choices.lesson: When prices rise and money doesn't, the same rupees buy less. That's inflation, so adjust the plan.
Ignoring price rises quietly drains your budget. Inflation is real even when it's small.

default.title: REFUND?
default.speaker: UPI request
default.text: 'Refund of ₹299 for your order! Approve this request with your UPI PIN to receive it.'

earner.title: REFUND?
earner.speaker: 'Customer'
earner.text: A 'customer' says he overpaid you and sends a request: 'Approve with your PIN to get my refund.'

choices.lesson: Entering your PIN always SENDS money. A refund never needs your PIN.
Right! A PIN means money going out. You never need it to receive.

default.title: PAID? REALLY?
default.speaker: Customer
default.text: A customer shows a 'Payment successful ₹350' screenshot and starts to leave. Your phone hasn't pinged.

scholarship.title: PAID? REALLY?
scholarship.speaker: Senior
scholarship.text: You're selling your old books. A senior flashes a 'Paid ₹350' screenshot and grabs them. No ping.

choices.lesson: A screenshot is a picture, not a payment. Only your own app or bank SMS proves money arrived.
Only your own app or bank SMS proves you were paid. Always check before you hand anything over.

default.title: TYRE BURST
default.speaker: Your cycle
default.text: Your cycle tyre bursts on the way to college. Repair: ₹150. You have no savings to fall back on.

choices.lesson: No buffer means every small shock becomes a loan. Even ₹50 a month adds up to a cushion.
No debt, but it hurt. A small buffer would have fixed it the same day.

effects.label: Fixed it; started saving ₹50 a month

choices.lesson: Paying for it was tough, but starting a buffer today means the next shock won't be.
